## polyPlot Overview

The following code introduces the statistical layers in a standard polyPlot and shows how a histogram or density curve can represent the underlying distribution.

```{r toc, echo=FALSE}
thisfile <- knitr::current_input()
revised_toc(thisfile, base_level = 3, toc_depth = 1)
```

---

### The Basic PolyPlot

First, simulate a set of 100 scores from a normal distribution. Then call `polyStats` to get the summary statistics and `polyPlot` to get the associated plot.

```{r, Overview-Default}
Scores <- round(rnorm(100, 10, 2), 0)
polyStats(Scores, digits = 3)
polyPlot(Scores)
```

### Adding a Distribution

To see the relationship between the polyplot and the underlying distribution, either a frequency distribution (histogram) or a density curve can be added in the background.

Use `polyPlot` to get the plot with a frequency histogram.
```{r, Overview-Histogram}
polyPlot(Scores, type = "frequency", main = "PolyPlot and Histogram")
```

Instead, use `polyPlot` to get the plot with a density curve.
```{r, Overview-Density}
polyPlot(Scores, type = "density", main = "PolyPlot and Density")
```
